salient_findings: Mass attached to the interventricular septum with focal contrast enhancement on CT
key_facts: No active lung lesions on chest radiograph
Mass originates from the left ventricular lateral wall

shortlist.label: Papillary fibroelastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Second most common primary cardiac tumor

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign cardiac tumor in adults

shortlist.label: Thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of asymptomatic left ventricular mass

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible cause of left ventricular mass

raw.rationale: The mass is described as a mobile, smooth, oval, pedunculated mass, which is consistent with the typical appearance of a left ventricular myxoma. The size and location of the mass also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Papillary fibroelastoma
rejected.why: Papillary fibroelastomas are typically smaller and more often found on the valves

rejected.label: Fibroma
rejected.why: Fibromas are usually found in the ventricular septum and are less likely to be pedunculated

rejected.label: Thrombus
rejected.why: The patient has no history of atrial fibrillation or other conditions that would increase the risk of thrombus formation

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are rare in the left ventricle and would not typically present as a pedunculated mass
